summary: Round 43 recheck, 16:13-16:30Z 29 Sep (19:13-19:30 MSK). 0 Kaggle calls, no browser, nothing built or submitted. The round-42 recheck was lost to the network drop (notes only), so this round did not inherit a partial answer. The lens is saturated: every item in v3 FINAL_REPORT (i) and in the v2 'Dropped' table already has a recheck by id (R2-R41). So I picked (a) one old conclusion that new 29 Sep data can test, and (b) two RESULTS.md rows with no earlier recheck (exp11 and exp14/exp15 have 0 grep hits). (A) The CI insertion-gate time mark: v3 R5 admission, the ledger's CI_lo 2.2 h model ('gate did NOT fire iff L_hi <= 10.2 h'), and PC25-07's proof-grade line of 9.6 h with its 'ins-tail?' footnote. Re-tested against the 29 Sep CI/non-CI pairs, CI's in-kernel time is 1.68-2.20 h (same-batch pairs 1.82-2.20 h). The 9.6 h line and the 10.2 h code boundary are UPHELD. exp87a's own insertion provably ran (9.48 - 1.68 = 7.80 h <= 8.0 h). New issue: the patched card script mk_card_1837.py (a19e1bd6) dropped the pre-registered R38-A5 T1 footnote 'ins-tail?' for L_lo > 9.6 h. It matters only for a 0.960 read whose last PENDING header is after 18:36:17Z (21:36 MSK), about 1-2%. The fix is one hand-added clause; no code or rule changes. (B) RESULTS exp11+pp, 'every post-proc stage helps on the unseen embryo' (LOEO 6bba->44b6, +0.0234 vs +0.0153 in-embryo). UPHELD as stated, but it does not answer the Cyrus question. It covers structural stages (gap5, direct8, post-hoc divisions) on our own detector, not the threshold knobs that make up exp87a's public-only thousandths (cap 6, K, DIS). The same v2.1 stack then read 0.899 on LB (probe 1). No pair change. (C) RESULTS exp14 (intensity-augmented fine-tune) and exp15 (two-model ensemble), rejected on in-embryo hold12 labs. The REASON was the wrong kind, because an in-embryo lab cannot see robustness to embryo shift. The VERDICT still stands: detector-side LB reads went 1 up (probe 2, +0.004) and 7 down, including SEC -0.002 on the K base (probe 54). All ticked files share x138's detector, so no detector-diverse hedge exists among the COMPLETE files that does not also carry cap 6 + K. No finding yields a build, dummy, slot use or pair change. The evening chain stays as logged: the exp89t read under decision B, the 18:37Z card, T7 at ~19:20Z, manual-admit at 19:44:45Z, the 19:43Z/21:05Z SELECTED checks and 00:07Z.

findings.what: OLD CONCLUSION: v3 FINAL_REPORT (e) R5 (a file is admitted only when its latency proves the timers did not degrade it). The CI-family ledger line says 'insertion gate did NOT fire iff L_hi <= 10.2 h', which is the in-kernel 8.0 h DIVINS gate plus CI_lo = 2.2 h. CI_lo was a model (>= 100 hidden videos x 158 s dummy mean / 2 workers; CONTEXT l.3135-3137, tools/runtime_ledger.py l.59). PC25-07 (28 Sep) found CI_lo contradicted by the measured dL of 1.60-2.18 h. It kept 10.2 h as the code boundary and added the footnote 'ins-tail?' for L in (9.6, 10.2] h (the proof-grade line; insertion possibly skipped on tail videos, <= ~0.0005). R38-A5 T1 carries it as 'ins-tail? if L_lo > 9.6 h'. WHAT CHANGED: the 29 Sep reads add pairs. exp89r (9.04, 9.22] vs exp89p (7.02, 7.20], submitted 40 min apart (DIS runtime = sibling) -> dL (1.84, 2.20). exp75 (8.88, 9.05] vs exp89p, same night -> (1.68, 2.03). exp75 vs #37 (7.36, 7.54], cross-day -> (1.34, 1.69). The earlier same-batch pair was exp79a (9.27, 9.45] vs exp78b (7.27, 7.45] -> (1.82, 2.18). exp89t (K + DIS + CI) is still PENDING at the 16:14:50Z header (L > 7.24 h). NEW VERDICT: UPHELD. The same-night and same-batch pairs put CI's in-kernel time at 1.68-2.20 h, so the proof-grade line is 8.0 + 1.68 = 9.68 h, about PC25-07's 9.6 h. The cross-day 1.34 h value mixes queue drift and does not bound CI time. The 8.0 h mark is itself conservative because L includes queue and scoring time. exp87a's insertion provably ran (L_hi 9.48 - 1.68 = 7.80 <= 8.0), and so did exp75's and exp89r's. For exp89t, a read with L_lo <= 9.6 h is clean. L_lo in (9.6, 10.2] h is a normal read with the 'ins-tail?' footnote (skip risk <= ~0.0005 on tail videos, which could be private ones). Above 10.2 h it is UNPROVEN-ins as coded. Under decision B this touches only a 0.960 read. P(0.960) <= ~0.11 (R38) and P(L_lo > 9.6 h) is ~10-20% (all CI files so far had L_hi 8.88-9.48 h), so the footnote case is ~1-2%. In that case the promotion's private edge (~+0.0004..+0.0006, R41-RC-A) and the worst-case tail skip (<= ~0.0005) are the same size. The logged rule still promotes; no carve-out now (it would be post-hoc).

findings.what: OLD CONCLUSION: experiments/RESULTS.md exp11+pp (early Sep, LOEO: detector fine-tuned on 6bba only, 12 unseen-embryo 44b6 videos): 'every post-proc stage helps on the unseen embryo'. Arm B: raw 0.8825 -> gap5 0.8934 -> +direct8 0.9014 -> v2 0.9059 (+0.0234). Arm A: 0.8798 -> 0.8963 (+0.0165). In-embryo hold12 (exp10): 0.9575 -> 0.9728 (+0.0153). This is the only in-house out-of-embryo read of post-processing, and it was never rechecked (0 grep hits). WHAT CHANGED: the 13:21Z private-risk audit and Cyrus/You WeiLin in 744273 argue that exp87a's post-proc thousandths (cap 6 +0.002, K +0.002, CI +0.001) are public-only. Is exp11 evidence against that? NEW VERDICT: UPHELD as stated, but not usable for the finals question. (1) It measures STRUCTURAL stages (gap closing, direct linking, post-hoc divisions): large, mechanism-driven gains of +0.005..+0.011 each. The public-tuned levers are THRESHOLD knobs (fork cap, ILP division weight, readmit score, disappearance weight) worth 0.001-0.002. (2) The same v2.1 stack (ILP div 0.6 + gap5 + direct8) read 0.899 on LB (probe 1) against hold12 0.9902. So 'post-proc transfers across embryos' did not even carry that stack's knob choices. (3) It used our own exp03B-line detector, not x138. So it neither rebuts nor supports the audit's label for cap 6 / DIS. For K, the out-of-embryo argument stands on R41-RC-B (the public embryo is itself unseen by the detector), not on exp11. П3 vs П2 remains the sign of CI on private (R37-RC-B, audit).

findings.what: OLD CONCLUSIONS: RESULTS exp14. A fine-tune (1200 it) with intensity augmentation (gain 0.5-1.6, offset -0.15..0.45, gamma 0.6-1.5, haze p 0.3) scored hold12 0.9345 vs exp03B 0.9575, det loss 0.017 vs 0.0022, and was 'rejected'. RESULTS exp15. The exp03B + exp08 logit ensemble (raw 0.9708 vs 0.9820) was 'rejected'. Neither was rechecked (0 hits). WHAT CHANGED: private = ~71% of the hidden test on other, unseen embryos. Intensity augmentation and ensembling are the textbook embryo-shift robustness levers. The hold12 lab is in-embryo (the same 44b6/6bba videos the models trained on), so it structurally cannot see a robustness gain. The REASON for rejection was therefore of the wrong kind. RE-CHECK against out-of-embryo evidence: the public embryo is unseen, and the detector-side LB record since then is 1 up and 7 down. Up: probe 2 (primary := exp03B fine-tune) +0.004. Down: probe 5 (secondary weight 0.5) -0.002, probe 7 (secondary := exp08) -0.016, probe 10 (scratch secondary) -0.025, probe 13 (fine-tuned secondary) -0.007, probe 16 (Z-flip TTA) -0.009, probe 17 (primary soup) -0.004, and probe 54 (SEC n2a on the K base, 29 Sep) -0.002. exp14's own training diverged (8x det loss), which is a failure, not a robustness trade-off. NEW VERDICT: the rejection STANDS; only its reason is corrected. Consequence for tonight: every ticked or tickable x138-family file shares x138's detector, so the pair has no detector-side hedge. The only COMPLETE detector-diverse files are exp89p (0.956) and exp89r (0.957). Both carry cap 6 + K and read below exp87a, so neither is a hedge partner (consistent with Q3: SEC only as V_pub). Retraining is closed and no slot remains, so there is nothing to build.
